newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle close stronger, cash up.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle close stronger, cash up.

text.p: Reports that cash fed cattle markets were trading at firmer prices, up to $68 per cwt in the southern Plains and $69 in Nebraska, prompted short covering that turned nearby CME live cattle futures up after early rolling of longs, traders said.
Feeder cattle followed with back months starting to show expectations of strong cash markets by fall, they said.
Live cattle closed 0.300 to 0.150 cent per lb higher with April up 0.300 at 68.700 cents. Feeder cattle ended up 0.275 to 0.625 with August up most and May up 0.425 at 69.350 cents.
Reports of packers paying higher prices for cash cattle sparked short covering demand in April live cattle late.
"There was talk on the floor of $69 trade in Nebraska" said Dan Vaught, livestock analyst for A.G. Edwards.
The USDA later confirmed Nebraska sales on a few cattle as high as $69 and active sales at $68 in the southern Plains, up $1 from recent transactions.

April had been pressured early by active rolling of longs into back months. The large open interest in April made longs nervous, especially with cash trade remaining slow early in the session, traders said. Many funds also need to move out of April before it becomes the spot month, they said.
